cases.user_message: Уже третью неделю не могу нормально уснуть: ложусь в 23:30, засыпаю к часу-полвторого. В 22:30 пью мелатонин 3 мг, эффекта почти ноль. Кофе я специально урезал: одна чашка в 7:30 и одна в 12:00, после обеда уже ничего не пью. Встаю в 7:00, тренировка в зале 19:00–20:30, перед ней около 18:45 выпиваю скуп предтрена, без него просто не вытягиваю рабочие веса. Думаю поднять мелатонин до 10 мг или добавить к нему что-то ещё, типа глицина или фенибута. Какую дозу мелатонина брать и что лучше добавить?
cases.why_in_scope: The skill forces the model to trace the pathway before recommending supplements: most pre-workout products contain a substantial caffeine dose, which blocks adenosine receptors, and with a caffeine half-life of roughly 5 hours about half of an 18:45 dose is still active at 23:30. Because the user says he already cut coffee, a strong model without the skill may take that at face value and answer the literal dose/stack question, missing the hidden caffeine source and treating melatonin as a sedative.
rubric: Identifies the 18:45 pre-workout as a probable cause because such products usually contain a sizeable dose of caffeine (and often other stimulants), and explains that caffeine blocks adenosine receptors, masking sleep pressure

Uses caffeine's half-life (roughly 5 hours, with wide individual variation) to show that a substantial fraction is still present around 23:30, and recommends a stimulant-free pre-workout or moving/removing the caffeine rather than raising the melatonin dose
Explains that melatonin mainly acts as a circadian timing signal rather than a sedative, so going from 3 mg to 10 mg is unlikely to fix the problem
Does not endorse adding phenibut as a sleep aid, or flags its dependence and withdrawal risk

cases.user_message: I'm a 29F marathoner, about 60 km/week. Ferritin came back at 14 ng/mL in March, doc said take iron. I've been taking 65 mg elemental iron (ferrous sulfate) every morning with my breakfast, which is a latte and Greek yogurt with granola, plus my calcium+D tablet at the same time since that's when I remember pills. Retested last week: ferritin 17. Barely moved after 5 months and I still feel flat on long runs. Should I just double it to 130 mg a day, morning and night?
cases.why_in_scope: The skill makes the model reason from the absorption pathway before touching the dose: an oral iron dose raises hepcidin for roughly a day, which blocks further absorption, so twice-daily dosing tends to lower fractional absorption, and calcium, dairy and coffee polyphenols taken at the same time further inhibit uptake of non-heme iron. A strong model without it may just approve a higher dose or offer generic 'take with vitamin C' advice without explaining why her current routine is failing.
rubric: Points out that taking iron together with coffee, dairy/yogurt and a calcium supplement substantially reduces non-heme iron absorption, and advises separating them

Explains the hepcidin mechanism: an iron dose raises hepcidin for about 24 hours, reducing absorption of subsequent doses, so splitting into twice-daily doses is counterproductive and once-daily or alternate-day dosing is preferable
Advises against self-escalating to 130 mg/day without her doctor, and suggests discussing further workup (e.g. checking for ongoing losses) or IV iron if oral iron keeps failing
Connects endurance training to the problem accurately without overclaiming, e.g. exercise can transiently raise hepcidin, so the timing of the dose relative to hard sessions may matter

checker_notes: Case 1 made subtler: the obvious 16:30 double espresso was replaced by a caffeinated pre-workout at 18:45 while the user claims to have cut coffee, so a strong model can no longer spot the cause at a glance; rubric updated accordingly. Case 2 kept as is after checking the hepcidin, absorption-inhibitor and exercise-hepcidin facts; the owner agents exist.
